# `star()` {#fn-star}

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-star)

```{=html}
<p>A historical comparison requires a stellar coordinate for the epoch under study. The
function resolves a Western common name through star.names or accepts a catalogue
identifier and checks it against Swiss Ephemeris. It evaluates equatorial coordinates at
noon UT on 1 January of each supplied astronomical year in the Gregorian calendar. The
magnitude is a catalogue value. These outputs can feed horizon transformations or
visibility estimates, which additionally require observer and atmosphere information.
</p>
<p>The Swiss Ephemeris manual documents fixed-star positions and catalogue magnitudes.
</p>
```

<details><summary>Method references</summary>

```{=html}
<p>Astrodienst. Swiss Ephemeris programmer's manual. <a href="https://www.astro.com/swisseph/swephprg.htm">https://www.astro.com/swisseph/swephprg.htm</a>.
</p>



```

</details>

**Interpretation and limits.** A named catalogue entry identifies a data source as well as a target. Preserve the resolved designation, epoch and catalogue version, especially for a multiple star or integrated cluster.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>string</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>This can be either the traditional name for the star or its Bayer designation.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>year</code></th><td><code>skyscapeR.env$cur.year</code></td><td><p>Year for which to calculate the coordinates. Historical labels such as <code>"3700 BC"</code> are accepted by <code>astroYear</code>.
Defaults to current year.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A skyscapeR.star list with name, Bayer designation, apparent magnitude (app.mag) and a coord data frame. Each row contains year, right ascension (RA) and declination (Dec), both angles in degrees.
</p>
```

</details>

**Implementation.** `R/stars.R`.
